sections.h2: How can a Marysville owner sell quickly?
sections.html:
In Marysville you can put the house on the market with a broker, find a buyer yourself, or take a straight cash purchase. Deed work at the Union County auditor and recorder follows whichever you choose.

Pick by weighing condition against calendar. A listing casts the widest net, and it also brings showings and a buyer's inspection report. A cash offer shrinks the sale to a single negotiation over price and closing day.

  • Agent: the broadest audience, paid for with a commission and repair haggling.
  • Owner-run: you save the commission and take over the marketing and contract work.
  • Cash: one number, fewer steps, and a closing day you can often choose.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Marysville housing?
sections.html:
Marysville's population is estimated at 30,190 for July 1, 2025, against 25,571 in the April 2020 count. QuickFacts shows the change since its 2020 estimates base at 17.9 percent.

QuickFacts prices the typical owner-occupied Marysville home at $300,800 for 2020-2024 and counts owners in 67.5 percent of units. Rent has a median of $1,223 a month, and owner costs have medians of $1,851 with a mortgage and $681 without one. The city has 10,163 households averaging 2.46 people, and median household income is $92,619.

Citywide medians say little about one address. Request a written review of recent sales near yours before you accept any number.

sections.h2: Why do people want to live in Marysville?
sections.html:
Marysville is the Union County seat, roughly 27 miles northwest of Columbus, and its employers keep buyers in the area. Scotts Miracle-Gro was founded here in 1868 and still has its headquarters in the city. Honda's Marysville Auto Plant, about six miles northwest, has built the Accord since 1982.

Nestle has a Product Technology Center on the west side, and Univenture and a Parker Hannifin plant are also based in the city. U.S. Route 33 runs four lanes through town, tying it to Interstate 75 and the I-270 outerbelt.

Tree-lined streets earned Marysville the nickname Shaded City by 1888. More than 300 acres of parks hold trails along Mill Creek, and the Union County Fair runs from late July into early August.

sections.h2: How does Marysville's weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals give Marysville 40.48 inches of precipitation and 24.0 inches of snow a year. Precipitation of at least 0.01 inch falls on about 126 days a year.

January lows average 20.6 degrees Fahrenheit, and the all-time record high is 109. Roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces take that range every year, so inspectors in Union County tend to look at them first.

If any of those items are near the end of their life, say so up front. A cash buyer will price the work, and a financed buyer will bring it up at inspection.

sections.h2: Which Marysville landmarks and neighborhoods shape a sale?
sections.html:
Samuel W. Culbertson laid out Marysville in 1819 beside Mill Creek and named it for his daughter Mary. The village incorporated in 1840, and in 2008 the city was designated a Preserve America Community.

The Union County Courthouse, built in 1883, still serves the county, and the Uptown square around it holds the library, the Scotts museum and city offices. Memorial Hospital of Union County arrived in the medical district in 1952, and the Union County Airport on the east side opened in 1967.

Timberview, an upscale section with a golf course, and Greenwood Colony both sit on the south side. Eljer and Lewis parks have lighted tennis courts, and the Marysville Journal-Tribune, dating to 1849, covers local sales and civic news.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a Marysville house?
sections.html:
Almost all of Marysville falls in the Marysville Exempted Village School District, with a few parcels reaching into Fairbanks Local. The district changes your tax bill, so verify it for the parcel.

The Union County auditor's GIS map includes a school district layer, and the auditor's FAQ explains one wrinkle: if a district line cuts through a house, the district holding the master bedroom taxes the entire house.

The auditor's parcel page has a "Where your taxes go" link that lists every levy and a Total Effective Rate.

sections.h2: What must a Marysville seller disclose?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure duty for houses with up to four units. The seller completes the state form, signs and dates it, and hands it to prospective buyers. It asks about water supply, sewage, roof and foundation, radon, lead paint, asbestos and other known defects.

The duty does not reach every transfer. Excluded sales include:

  • Court-ordered transfers and fiduciary transfers for an estate or trust.
  • Transfers to a spouse or direct-line relatives.
  • Heirs who never lived in the house during the previous year.

A buyer handed the form late may cancel in writing for three business days after receiving it. That right lapses 30 days after acceptance or at closing, if sooner.

sections.h2: What happens at the Union County auditor and recorder?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5301.01 has the seller sign the deed and acknowledge it before a notary or similar officer. The deed then goes to the Union County Auditor at 233 W. Sixth St. in Marysville, where the buyer's side files a value statement (DTE 100) or an exemption statement (DTE 100EX).

The seller settles the conveyance fee, so ask the auditor which rate applies before closing day. Mailed conveyances reach the recorder only with the auditor's stamp already applied, and the recorder's posted charge for a deed is $39.00 through page two, then $8.00 a page.

sections.h2: When are Union County complaints and exemption notices due?
sections.html:
A Board of Revision complaint on a Union County parcel must reach the auditor after January 1 and on or before March 31. Other posted dates and amounts appear in the table.

Union County items for Marysville owners

  • The 2.5 percent rollback covers owner-occupied homes, one property per owner, and requires an application.
  • A requested change above $50,000 of market value, or $17,500 assessed, sends notice to the school board.
  • After a recent sale, attach the closing statement, contract and deed to support your complaint.

sections.h2: Do Marysville improvements need permits before a sale?
sections.html:
Marysville requires a zoning permit for most additions: decks, fences, swimming pools, sheds, garages and room additions, plus public sidewalks and driveway approaches built by a contractor licensed with the city. Some jobs also need a building permit from the Union County Building Department.

Ask the city zoning office about any structure on your lot that lacks one. Old decks and sheds show up on inspections, and a cash buyer will price in whatever cleanup remains.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale suit a Marysville owner?
sections.html:
It suits owners who value a quick, certain close over the last few thousand dollars of price. Common cases:

  • An inherited house nobody plans to occupy.
  • An aging roof, furnace or foundation.
  • Tenants who make showings hard to schedule.
  • A job move on a fixed date.

Set any offer beside what a listing would leave you after repair bills, commission and months of upkeep.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marysville house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale, but problems you know about belong on the disclosure form. A cash purchaser accepts the house as found, while a buyer with a lender may ask for fixes.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Marysville sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the grantor settles it before the auditor endorses the deed.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Marysville property value?
faqs.a: Union County takes these complaints from January 1 to March 31, for the current tax year only. A notarized complaint goes to the auditor by email, fax or mail.

faqs.q: Does an inherited Marysville house need the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Frequently not. Transfers by an estate's fiduciary are excluded, as are sales by heirs who never occupied the house in the previous year.

faqs.q: How do I find the tax rate for a Marysville parcel?
faqs.a: Look up the parcel on the Union County auditor's website. The Total Effective Rate column under "Where your taxes go" gives the rate for that district.
